amendment.text: San Antonio leaves the toilet ratios of Table 403.1, the half-and-half split (403.1.1), the single-user rule (403.1.2), the small-occupancy exceptions (403.2 exceptions 2 to 5) and the urinal substitution rule (424.2) as the 2024 International Plumbing Code prints them. Its only changes in Section 403 are table note e (service sinks) and exception 6 of Section 403.2 on rooms shared by all sexes, which now asks for "walls and a door enclosing the fixtures" for water closets and urinals in place of the model code's reference to the partition privacy sections 405.3.4 and 405.3.5. The building code's parallel exception (2902.2 exception 6) is amended the same way and drops the urinal sentence. Because Texas has no statewide table, the page needs its own stall table, read from the 2024 code as San Antonio adopted it.
amendment.quote: Table 403.1, MINIMUM NUMBER OF REQUIRED PLUMBING FIXTURES, note e is deleted in its entirety and replaced with the following text and shall apply to all Classifications in the Table: e. Service sinks are not required for an occupant load of 15 or fewer or as otherwise approved by the code official. || Section 403.2, Separate facilities, Exception 6 is amended as follows, all other code text remains as is: Exceptions: 6. Separate toilet facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by all persons regardless of sex and privacy is provided for water closets and urinals [in accordance with Section 405.3.4. and for urinals in accordance with Section 405.3.5] with walls and a door enclosing the fixtures.

table_ratios.office: Business: water closets 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 (each sex)
table_ratios.restaurant: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts: 1 per 75 male, 1 per 75 female
table_ratios.split: 403.1.1: "To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number."
table_ratios.urinals: None required. 424.2: "In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets for males according to Table 403.1 in all other occupancies."
table_ratios.small_occupancy: 403.2 exception 2: "Separate toilet facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer." Exception 4: business occupancies of 25 or fewer. Exception 3: mercantile of 100 or fewer.
table_ratios.source: Secondary copy: UpCodes, San Antonio Plumbing Code 2024 (the 2024 International Plumbing Code with the city's amendments merged in). The official ICC viewer loads its text by script and could not be read.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Half the occupants counted as each sex, fractions rounded up (403.1.1). Office at 200: 100 each sex, 2 for the first 50 plus 1 for the next 50. Office at 400: 200 each sex, 2 plus 3. Restaurant at 400: 200/75 = 2.67, so 3. Urinals may replace up to 50% of the men's toilets in offices and up to 67% in restaurants and schools (424.2). An office of 25 or fewer needs no separate rooms (403.2 exception 4); for other uses the limit is 15, so the 50 row keeps separate rooms.

Any owner or authorized agent who intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish, or change the occupancy of a building or structure, to include a sign or billboard, or to erect, install, enlarge, alter, repair, remove, convert or replace any electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system, the installation of which is regulated by this chapter, who performs site work or causes any such work to be done, shall first make application to the Building Official and obtain the required permit.

This work does not require a permit by themselves but are generally included with permits with more extensive work." Toilet partitions, which are anchored to the floor, wall or ceiling, are not named in the code, in Information Bulletin 189 or on the permit process page, and none of them says whether replacing them is "similar finish work" or a repair.

restrooms_city.rule: No separate city ordinance on single-user restroom signs or all-gender rooms was found. The city's code amendments change one thing: a room shared by all sexes is allowed in place of separate men's and women's rooms where the water closets and urinals have "walls and a door enclosing the fixtures" (plumbing code 403.2 exception 6 as amended; the building code's 2902.2 exception 6 says the same for water closets and drops its urinal sentence). The model code's reference to the partition privacy sections is struck out. Single-user rooms follow the unamended 2024 code: identified as available to all persons regardless of sex. Two other city restroom rules were found on the way: a baby changing station in public restrooms of assembly and mercantile buildings, hospitals and city buildings when a restroom is built, enlarged by 50 square feet or more or given more fixtures (building code 1210.4 as added), and a domestic violence resource sign in every restroom of a public place (City Code Sec. 15-285, posting required by October 1, 2024).
restrooms_city.quote: Section 2902.2, Separate facilities, Exception 6 is amended as follows, all other code text remains as is: 6. Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets [in accordance with Section 405.3.4 of the International Plumbing Code. Urinals shall be located in an area visually separated from the remainder of the facility or each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall] with walls and a door enclosing the fixtures. || 403.1.2 (unamended, UpCodes copy): "Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex." || 1210.4 Baby changing stations. Each publicly available and accessible restroom serving Group A and Group M occupancy type areas, hospitals, and city owned buildings shall be equipped with a minimum of one (1) safe, sanitary, and convenient baby changing station under the following circumstances: 1. New building ... 2. Existing building ... and any of the following changes are made: a. A new restroom is built b. The square footage of an existing restroom is increased by fifty (50) square feet or more c. The number of fixtures of an existing restroom is increased
restrooms_city.dv_signs_quote: City health department page (fetch tool): signs go in "all female, male, unisex, and family restrooms used by the public or employees"; posting was required by October 1, 2024.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to San Antonio job sites. Price your restroom, pick the right material and see the San Antonio and Texas rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for San Antonio offices, schools, hotels and restaurants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** San Antonio's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** San Antonio sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** San Antonio requires a permit to alter or repair a building unless the work is exempt. Its exempt list covers "similar finish work" and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high, without naming toilet partitions, so ask San Antonio Development Services whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. In a private building, San Antonio allows a shared all-gender room where every toilet and urinal is enclosed by walls and a door. The city's rules say walls, not partitions, so ask San Antonio Development Services what it accepts before you plan one. Since December 2025, Texas law requires shared restrooms in city, county, school district and public college buildings to be designated for one sex.
page.stalls_intro: San Antonio counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional. They may stand in for up to half of the men's toilets in an office, and up to two thirds in a restaurant or school.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building. An office that holds 25 people or fewer, or any other space that holds 15 or fewer, staff and customers together, doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or San Antonio Development Services sets the final number.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Baby changing stations and restroom signs:** San Antonio requires a baby changing station in public restrooms of restaurants, stores, event venues, hospitals and city buildings when a restroom is built, enlarged by 50 square feet or more or given more fixtures. Public places must also post a domestic violence resource sign in every restroom.
page.install_rule: San Antonio has no license or registration requirement for commercial general contractors. It registers residential building, home improvement and trade contractors. Texas has no statewide contractor license for this work. Confirm what your project needs with San Antonio Development Services. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: San Antonio has no license or registration requirement for commercial general contractors.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on city, county and school district projects, Texas law requires at least the locally set wage. The federal rate for a carpenter on building work in Bexar County is $16.86 an hour plus $4.17 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.25% in San Antonio: 6.25% state, 1.125% city, 0.5% transit authority and 0.375% advanced transportation district.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels, convention venues and River Walk restaurants:** phenolic or stainless steel for guest restrooms that stay busy all day and are cleaned often.
